diffs.diff: header pin 10 (SER): part says gnd, datasheet reading says io
diffs.evidence: TI SN74HC165 datasheet (SCLS116), Pin Functions table: 'SER 10 I Serial Input', so the pin's position (10) and name match and it is a logic input, not a ground pin. The two readings agree on the pin; they differ only in how it is wired. In this model, role 'gnd' is the app's way of saying 'strap this pin to GND' (autowire.ts connects role-gnd pins to the board's GND; 74HC595 OE uses the same convention). The datasheet requires that: Recommended Operating Conditions note (1), 'All unused inputs of the device must be held at VCC or GND to ensure proper device operation.' For the single chip this part models, SER is unused and is held at GND, so it shifts in 0s. If the role were 'io' with required:true, autowire would put SER on a free GPIO that the example never sets up, leaving a CMOS input floating. The pin description and SKILL.md still say to wire it to the next chip's QH when chaining. Caveat: in a daisy-chain, the GND-strap role makes the checker report a false 'no ground connection' on SER.

diffs.diff: header pin 15 (CLK INH): part says gnd, datasheet reading says io
diffs.evidence: TI SN74HC165 datasheet (SCLS116), Pin Functions table: 'CLK INH 15 I Clock Inhibit, when High No change in output'. Description: 'Clocking is accomplished ... when CLK INH is held low.' The pin number and name match and it is an input. Role 'gnd' in this model means 'strap to GND', and the datasheet requires that for normal clocking: CLK INH must be low for CLK to shift. Holding the input at GND also satisfies note (1), 'All unused inputs ... must be held at VCC or GND.' The example's HC165(load, clock, data) uses no clk_inh GPIO, so tying CLK INH to GND is the correct wiring for this model. Marking it 'io' would let autowire put it on an unconfigured GPIO, where it floats and can block shifting.
